lines.text: Yeah baby believe this yeah Yeah saints on
the bus with the windows cracked
Storm in the sky but the wheels stay
black Corona Gita Bible and the art of
war All in my bag like I've been
here before 23 still hungry still holy still
haunted Halo half lit where the hard streets
taunted Headed for the water where the world
lines roar And the sky kept asking what's
the metaphor At 23 I walked where sirens
prayed The cracked concrete became a party seat
My mother marked my forehead unafraid And whispered
child let God decide the key The billboards
blinked like prophets selling doom The cameras bowed
like vultures in the rain A thousand as
new names inside my room And dressed their
lies in algorithmic flame The handshakes had hands
hidden in hands The choir had wires woven
in the walls The saints sang soft of
promised lands While drones drew halos over project
halls But I kept songs in pockets prayers
in cold A sacred sentence stitched beneath my
tongue The crooked compass trembled on the road
Like time itself had heard what I had
sung Pastor said there's thunder in your name
Deacon said don't bargain with the flood Driver
said this route is not the same Then
lightning signed the dashboard with my blood We
rode through the Bermuda rain On a gospel
bus with a ghostly flame Time bent low
when the thunder came And Jesus called me
by my name Baby believe this baby believe
this When the two tips flash and the
heavens roar Ask your soul what's the metaphor
Baby believe this baby believe this Twenty three
with a prophecy sewn Through the triangle where
the bridegate shone Baby what's the metaphor Mercy
marching through a locked front door What's the
metaphor Poor boy chosen for a holy war
What's the metaphor Truth in the storm that
the rich ignore What's the metaphor God was
the driver the whole time Lord The Baptist
bus had Catholics in the back A Muslim
kid with moonlight in his stare A Hindu
girl with saffron on her track And one
old monk who vanished in a prayer Some
carry beads and some carry bruises Some carry
secrets the city refused Some saw angels in
emergency lights Some saw demons in satellite news
We passed three ships in a spiral of
years One sail with soldiers one sail with
myths One had a billboard that whispered obey
Then sold us our nightmares at half price
pay The ocean opened its obsidian eye The
moon made a mouth in the mouth of
the sky The clock caught blood and the
minutes reversed And every last wound sang a
hymn in the hearse A girl in the
back began humming amen The windows went white
then went black then again The preacher stood
tall with his hand on the rail Like
Moses had water with Jonah's well Then I
saw a city where the poor don't bleed
Where no child begs and no landlord fees
Where the last kneel first and the first
learn shame Where the real Jesus walks with
no brand name fame He wasn't gold he
wasn't for sale No billboard crown no sponsored
veil Dust on his robe fire in his
eyes He said they can watch but they
can't on skies We rode through the Bermuda
rain On a gospel bus with a ghostly
flame Time bent low when the thunder came
And Jesus called me by my name Baby
believe this yo Baby believe this yo When
the tooltip slash and the heavens roar Ask
your soul what's the metaphor Baby believe this
yo Baby believe this yo Twenty three with
a prophecy stoned Through the triangle where the
bright gate shone He showed me wars and
war of frilly fate He showed me kings
who kissed the poor for sure He showed
me every hidden hand in place Then showed
me how to let the hatred go He
said prophecy is not your panic Power is
not your rage Mercy is militant magic Love
is lightning on the page He said the
watcher cannot make you weak The liar cannot
make you blessed The cameras cannot steal the
meek The storm cannot unbless the blessed So
I came back breathing with a scar shaped
song A thunderbolt tucked in my open palm
The city still stared but it stared too
late I had bread for the hungry and
keys to the gate I had hymns for
the hurt and a house for the lost
I had names of the poor carved into
the cross I had fire not fury I
had faith not fame And the real Jesus
still called my name What's the metaphor Maybe
the scream was never the Lord What's the
metaphor Maybe the wound became the sword What's
the metaphor Maybe the map was made from
sky What's the metaphor Maybe the saints were
steering sky What's the metaphor Maybe the poor
inherit more What's the metaphor Maybe heaven hid
inside the war Hands in hands the body
guides Screens may scan but souls stay broad
Storms may stalk and systems see But no
machine can master me
